Eleven new files under /Users/maximilianthuemmler/Documents/last-city-nightfall/game/view/feel/ (2,144 lines) plus 6 test suites and 2 standalone scenes in tests/feel/ (2,091 lines).

THE SHARED LIBRARY (what other parts should use)
- ease.gd (LcnEase): 23 curves in two explicitly separated families — TRANSITIONS (0→1 interpolators incl. BACK_OUT, SETTLE, ANTICIPATE, spring) and ENVELOPES (IMPACT, PULSE, SPIKE, strength-over-lifetime). Pure math, deterministic.
- timing.gd (LcnTiming): THE TIMING VOCABULARY — seven named rungs, each paired with its curve: FLICK 0.06/QUART_OUT, SNAP 0.12/EXPO_OUT, QUICK 0.20/CUBIC_OUT, SETTLE 0.32/SETTLE, HEAVY 0.55/CUBIC_IN_OUT, SWELL 0.90/QUART_OUT, EVENT 2.60/SINE_IN_OUT. Plus the two clocks (world time for simulated effects, interface time for cursor response) and `decorative()`/`meaningful()`/`shake_scale()`/`hit_stop_enabled()` so accessibility is part of the vocabulary rather than a switch beside it. Documented in game/view/feel/README.md.
- tween_kit.gd (LcnTweenKit): pop / fade_in / fade_out / slide_in / count / deny / flash_modulate, house curves baked in, reduce-motion collapses to a cut.
- impulse.gd, number_ticker.gd, fx_pool.gd: a kick-and-recover scalar that survives interruption, a number that travels instead of snapping, and a fixed-size allocation-free effect store.

THE LAYER ITSELF (LcnFeel, group `lcn_feel`, self-installs via game/content/feel/feel_bootstrap.tres)
- Placement: a SETTLE stamp that snaps from 1.9x onto the footprint with corner brackets, a dust puff, a snap ring, a 0.06 camera impulse. Completion is warmer and larger (ring + flash + embers) because the player waited for it.
- Destruction/damage: spinning debris + heavy dust + 0.16 shake on demolition; sparks/flash/shake scaled by damage amount, with bounded hit-stop (90 ms at 0.28x, once per 0.6 s, never under the harness) above the heavy threshold.
- Hover/selection: a real lift — the same atlas sprite redrawn 5 px higher on a BACK_OUT spring with a growing shadow and a warm rim — plus corner brackets in FLICK and a slow-breathing selection. All on interface time, so it answers a paused game. `LcnFeel.focus_structure(id)` lets [P21] point it at a building.
- Nightfall as an EVENT: a soft-edged band crossing the frame on SINE_IN_OUT over 2.6 s, a low 8 Hz camera rumble, and a CONTINUOUS cold vignette keyed to [P13]'s own phase names so the player feels the hour for minutes, not one frame. Threat pressure breathes faster the closer a wave is.
- Idle life: warm structures breathe on a period derived from the heat they actually produce; pipes pulse with a phase from the cell coordinate so the bright band travels along a run (clearly visible in artifacts/p15_gallery/02_hover_lift.png).
- Every beat is re-emitted on `LcnFeel.beat(name, strength, at)` for [P23] audio and [P13] grade to hang cues on (place, complete, demolish, freeze, deny, hit, kill, select, alert, nightfall, dawn, assault, relief, law, research, game_over).

The mandated grep (`^ERROR|SCRIPT ERROR|add_child|formatting`) returns ONE line: "ERROR: 268 resources still in use at exit" — Godot's own shutdown notice, present in the pre-change baseline at 269. No SCRIPT ERROR, no add_child failure, no String formatting error from anything I touched.

2. Frame cost, measured not promised. Live reference run (log lines in artifacts/p15/log.txt): `feel] frame 0.032-0.054 ms | fx 50 alive / 50 drawn 0.372-0.442 ms | idle 44 anchors 0.182-0.230 ms | hover 0.002 ms | screen 0.002 ms`. Worst case in tests/feel/feel_perf.tscn (full 256-effect pool refilled every frame, 900-building city, every screen treatment lit): _process 70 us avg / 88 us max, _draw 641 us avg / 1466 us max = 4.3% of a 16.6 ms frame. The suite fails the build if that drifts.

3. Tests: `--part=feel` → 6 suites, 59 tests, 1627 asserts, 0 failed. tests/feel/feel_gallery.tscn → 24 checks pass (headless assertions + 13 PNGs with a display, artifacts/p15_gallery/); it builds a real session with the real renderer and camera, places and demolishes through Sim.submit_command, and RUNS THE WORLD FORWARD 6400 ticks until [P09]'s climate declares nightfall rather than faking the signal. tests/feel/feel_perf.tscn → 6 checks pass.

I looked at the frames myself (artifacts/p15_gallery/): the hover brackets and lift read cleanly on the hearth, the pipe pulse reads as flow along a run, the demolition dust and the impact sparks are visible, the frost hexagons are unmistakable, the threat vignette reads as pressure, and the night vignette holds after the sweep has passed.

FIVE BUGS MY OWN TESTS FOUND AND I FIXED: the IMPACT envelope had a zero-guard that made every flash fade IN; ELASTIC_OUT overshot 35% and broke the band every other curve lives in; the night-pressure table matched on `&"evening"`, a phase name [P13]'s palette never emits, so deep night carried no vignette at all (tests/feel/test_night_pressure.gd now walks every hour of the day); the idle-life rebuild timer ran on world time, so a paused or harness-driven session rebuilt the anchor list every single frame; and the nightfall sweep gradient put a hard horizontal line across the whole frame — visible in the first gallery pass, gone in the second.

The visual harness screenshot path is intermittently, hugely slow — a single shot can spend 2700+ frames waiting on RenderingServer.frame_post_draw. I A/B'd it with my layer removed entirely: run 1 took 2 frames, run 2 took 2995, run 3 took 2. It is pre-existing and environmental (likely GPU/window contention with the other agents' concurrent Godot windows), not caused by [P15] — but it cost three of my runs their timeout before I proved it, and it will do the same to the next agent. Worth someone owning.

World effects age on SimClock, so the 7-shot reference run will almost never catch a 0.32 s dust puff — six ticks out of eleven thousand. That is why tests/feel/feel_gallery.tscn exists and why the visual proof lives in artifacts/p15_gallery/ rather than artifacts/p15/shots/.

Hit-stop never touches Engine.time_scale when Harness.active, so automated runs exercise its state machine but not its effect. It is verified by unit test and by the reduce-motion gallery beat, not by a screenshot.

Idle life switches off below camera zoom 0.42 and culls to the view, so the strategic-zoom frames of the reference run show no breathing. Intentional (individual breaths merge into noise up there) but it means the deep_night reference shot understates the layer.
